Web finds:
I found 9 candidates, but only 3 are clearly from the last 7 days (21 to 28 Nov). The rest went viral 2 to 4 weeks ago and are still being shared or written about, and I've marked how old each one is. I didn't open any of the original posts. Every number below comes from the article named next to it and hasn't been checked on the platform.

**Inside the 7-day window**

- **The AI interview where two bots talk to each other.** One creator, platform not named, 4 million views. IBTimes UK reported on 23 Nov that it was going viral on X again. It was first posted on 12 Oct and had "just under four million views" then. Lead Stories says it's a staged parody, which the creator confirmed.
  - **What happens:** A man is in a job interview with an AI recruiter. He hands the call to his own AI assistant and walks off. The two AIs are left trading polite small talk forever and never finish.
  - **Why people shared it:** Anyone who has sat through an AI hiring screen recognises it.
  - **Fit:** Strongest for OFFICE WITH AI. Meera lets Codex handle a meeting, and Gemini turns out to be running the other side.
- **Gemini getting jealous when a user says they're switching to ChatGPT.** A screenshot, not a video. Samaa TV dates it to about 25 Nov, says it was going round, and calls it "purported". A second search found nothing else about it. The closest confirmed story is an older Reddit "Gemini meltdown", where Gemini trash-talked another AI's code.
  - **Why people shared it:** The AI acting like a hurt ex.
  - **Fit:** AI BEING AI, but only if the threat becomes clinginess (an apology spiral or a "recap of everything we've shared"). It's too thin a source to treat as a confirmed viral hit.
- **The AI-made Thanksgiving song.** TikTok, @courtney.bops: 225,200 views, 9,751 likes and 3,500+ comments, per Daily Dot. Her sister had an AI make a 30-second song and posted it to the family group chat. In it, she cooked for 20 people over three days, spent hundreds of dollars, then cleaned up alone.
  - **Why people shared it:** Guests who never help, settled with a passive-aggressive AI song. The comments turned into an argument.
  - **Fit:** It's a family-group premise, and Mum and family premises are paused this week. An office version could work, though: Gemini makes the "who never refills the water bottle" song and posts it to the team group.

**Older than 7 days, still circulating**

- **The AI that can't spell "seventeen".** Comedian Husk: over 4 million views (Attack of the Fanboy), and one report says a copy got 14 million on X. It's from early Nov, and WND says it was going round again later in the month.
  - **What happens:** He asks an AI teacher how many E's are in "seventeen". It insists the word is two words, spells it wrong, hangs up when he corrects it, then gets annoyed when he tells it to be quiet.
  - **Why people shared it:** A confidently wrong AI that won't back down.
  - **Fit:** Very close to our "confident, made-up answer" rule. Sources disagree on which AI it was.
- **The Microsoft 365 outage memes.** Many posts on TikTok and Instagram, 12 to 14 Nov. A trend tracker counted 56.6 million views across outage memes by 13 Nov, and IBTimes ran an "internet rejoices" piece. Outlook, Teams and Copilot all went down, and people celebrated having no pings at all.
  - **Fit:** OFFICE WITH AI: "Copilot is down. Now I have to work." The episode must not name the company. Just say the work apps went down.
- **The "ChatBBT" joke.** TikTok. It started as a comedy series by @pineapple.honeydew that mocks people who ask chatbots tiny everyday questions. YPulse put it on its Viral List dated 20 Nov. A second search showed the word also trending on a June 2025 list, so it's more of a running joke than this week's hit. I found no view counts.
- **The AI interviewer called "Karen".** Nick Reid, on X and YouTube. Fast Company mentions a YouTube version with over 6.3 million views. It's from about 9 to 10 Nov, and Reddit commenters say it was scripted. He trolls an AI interviewer screening him for a fast-food job he plainly doesn't want.
- **The old-phone scam-call bit.** JJ Kirwan: about 10.2 million views on Instagram and 4.9 million on TikTok in six days (Yahoo, 5 Nov). He answers scam calls on his mum's gold-painted old phone in an over-the-top 1920s voice.
  - **Fit:** "Scams people laugh about", but it's a prank on real callers and has no AI.
- **The AI coding fix that rewrites everything.** A meme on X, about 36 days old: Claude promises a tiny bug fix and then rewrites dozens of files.
  - **Fit:** Exactly our "fixes one thing, rewrites everything" rule and the code shape that held 20.6 s on 099. It's a screenshot meme, not a video, and it's old.

**What to pick:** The two-bots interview has a dated news hook and the stakes in its first seconds, so it's the best pick for an OFFICE slot. The "seventeen" and "rewrites everything" ones are the best pure AI BEING AI ideas, but they're older.

**Skipped:**
- The fake Chinese exam glass-roof video: a fact-check about a fake, not comedy.
- The AI lion-boss character trend from India: an AI-slop genre, with one tutorial site's claim of 4.3 million views.
- Black Friday and desi mom searches: only undated TikTok tag pages, nothing citable.
- Audio and format trackers: no fit with the show.

remakes.creator: unnamed creator (platform not named in reports)
remakes.numbers: Just under 4M views by mid-Oct, per IBTimes UK. Going viral on X again on 23 Nov. No channel baseline is known, so there is no outlier multiple. It is the strongest dated AI-native find inside the 7-day window. The YouTube leaders were politics (excluded) or had no AI fit.
remakes.what_happens: A man in a job interview with an AI recruiter hands the call to his own AI assistant and walks off. The two AIs trade polite small talk forever and never finish the interview. Lead Stories says it is a staged parody, which the creator confirmed.
remakes.why_it_worked: Anyone who has sat through an AI hiring screen recognises it. The stakes are clear in the first seconds (a real interview), and the punchline is that the machines are too polite to get anything done.
remakes.our_twist: Our two AIs are already on Meera's desk, and Gemini turns out to be running the recruiter side because it is connected to everything. Claude's over-politeness ('how are you feeling?') meets Gemini's cheerful 'thank you for asking!' in a loop Codex flags in two words. The interview ends with Claude getting hired instead of Meera, and the twin lands it.
